answer: Only 1 of the 18 original studies in the Experimental Economics replication project (project == "ee") was conducted in the United Kingdom — a proportion of 1/18 ≈ 5.6%. Hypothesis: According to the meta-regression study dataset (meta-regression_study_data_heterogeneity_in_replication_projects.csv), filtering rows where project == "ee" yields 18 unique original studies (18 unique id values, one per O/R pair; no duplicates by id or title, and no drop == True rows). Using the column experiment_country.o ("Country where original experiment was conducted"), exactly one original study has country == "United Kingdom": ee.13, "Deferred compensation in multiperiod labor contracts: an experimental test of Lazear's model" (Huck, Seltzer & Wallace, 2011, American Economic Review; lab-based, online.o = 0). The remaining 17 studies were run elsewhere: United States (11), Germany (2), Switzerland (2), Australia (1), Austria (1). There are no missing values in experiment_country.o within the ee subset and no non-standard spellings ("UK", "England", etc.) — only "United Kingdom" appears. Therefore the proportion of original Experimental Economics studies conducted in the United Kingdom is 1/18 ≈ 5.6% (about 1 in 18, i.e., under 6%), reflecting that ee-project originals are dominated by US-based laboratories (61% of studies).
